f1.quote: Expose the high-entropy nanoalloys to prolonged high-temperature conditions under controlled atmospheric environments.

f3.quote: Controlled high-temperature environment (e.g., elevated temperatures comparable to service conditions) with a defined atmosphere (e.g., inert or reducing gases) to prevent oxidation effects.

f7.quote: The lattice distortion in high-entropy nanoalloys creates energy barriers for atomic migration, slowing diffusion processes that would otherwise lead to phase segregation, coarsening, and chemical degradation.

f10.quote: Under high-temperature exposure, high-entropy nanoalloys will show significantly reduced grain growth, phase separation, and chemical inhomogeneity compared to low-entropy (binary or simpler) nanoalloys.
